title: Clinic appointment booking in a single DynamoDB table
name: Clinic appointment booking

defect.snippet: Item: { pk: providerPk(a.clinicId, a.providerId), sk: slotSk(a.slotStart), ...a },

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code models and writes appointment slots? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The provider slot Put has no ConditionExpression. The patient-side item always has a fresh sk (it includes the new appointmentId), so its attribute_not_exists check never fails. Two patients booking the same provider slot concurrently (or one after another) both succeed: the second Put silently overwrites the provider's SLOT item, while both patients keep an appointment record. The slot Put needs ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(pk)".

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does book() write the appointment twice, once under the provider key and once under the patient key?
choices: To keep a backup copy in case one item is deleted
Because DynamoDB requires every item to be reachable from two keys
Because a transaction must touch at least two items
So both access patterns (a provider's day, a patient's upcoming visits) are single-partition Queries without a scan or secondary index
choiceQuestions.explanation: providerDay queries the provider pk with begins_with(sk, 'SLOT#date'), and patientUpcoming queries the patient pk with sk >= APPT#from. Duplicating items per access pattern is standard NoSQL modeling. It isn't a backup, DynamoDB has no two-key requirement, and single-item transactions are allowed.

choiceQuestions.prompt: How does providerDay('c1', 'p9', '2026-03-02') select the right appointments?
choices: It scans the table filtering on slotStart
Slot sort keys are 'SLOT#' + ISO timestamp, so begins_with 'SLOT#2026-03-02' matches every slot that day
It reads a separate day-index item
It relies on a GSI keyed by date
choiceQuestions.explanation: BookingService normalizes slotStart with toISOString, so sort keys look like SLOT#2026-03-02T09:15:00.000Z and a prefix match on the date picks up exactly that day. No scan, day item, or GSI is involved.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The booking transaction succeeds but recordAudit throws (e.g. a throttling error). What does the caller observe?
choices: BookingService.book rejects with the error even though the appointment items were written
The appointment is rolled back because the audit is part of the transaction
book returns { ok: true } and the audit failure is ignored
choiceQuestions.explanation: recordAudit runs after the transaction, outside the try/catch, so its error propagates to the caller while the appointment is already committed. It isn't in the transaction, isn't a SlotConflictError, and isn't swallowed.
